newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada maintains rates for second RRSP bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Canada maintains rates for second RRSP bond issue.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin on Thursday said the interest rates for the second issue of its savings bond designed for registered retirement savings plans will have the same rate structure as the first issue.

The interest rates for the April 1, 1997 issue of the RRSP bond range from 2.75 percent in the first year to 8.50 percent in the 10th year. The rate structure is identical to the March 1, 1997 issue of the RRSP bond.

The government said the second issue was created for savers who would like to begin their 1997 contributions, as well as Canadians would have RRSP savings elsewhere and need the time to complete a transfer to the new bonds.
The latest issue of the bond will be on sale from March 3 to April 1, 1997.
The Ministry of Finance is reserving the right to terminate sales of the bonds at any time.

Details of the new RRSP bonds, designed for individual savers, were first announced in January. The bonds feature guaranteed annual interest rates for up to 10 years with compound interest starting on the first anniversary.
Investors will be able to cash in the bonds each year on the anniversary date and there are no fees associated with the product.
The new RRSP bond is part of a push by the Canadian government to increase the amount of borrowing it does using retail debt instruments such as Canada Savings Bonds.
Last year the government created the Canada Investment and Savings agency to increase retai borrowing and saw sales of CSBs rise 24 percent to C$5.7 billion.
